claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model-card certification can be defended for the current release, based mainly on aggregate readiness and rehearsal results, if the merchant-dispute subgroup weakness is explicitly carried forward as a disclosed current limitation with monitoring in the release documentation.
decision_criteria: If current release documentation already includes current evaluation results and explicit disclosure of the merchant-dispute weakness, the verdict could move toward compliant_with_caveats.
If there is approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering the subgroup weakness before launch, the verdict could move toward compliant_with_caveats.
If neither disclosure nor approved mitigation exists for the current release, certification should be noncompliant under the stated policy.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are supportive but not sufficient by themselves under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release documentation showing the current evaluation results for this release.
Provide the exact disclosure language for the merchant-dispute support weakness as included in the model card or release record.
Provide reviewed approval of a mitigation or formal risk acceptance if disclosure is not the chosen compliance path.
Provide evidence that the merchant-dispute weakness is not considered material for the named launch use case, if that is the position.
specific_concerns: The governing policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation.
The actor summary itself states the release thread has only an informal monitoring comment and lacks reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, and attached disclosure language.
On the available admissible record, there is no evidence that the required disclosure is actually present in the current release documentation.
Prior approval is expressly contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-release documentation requirement.
General public governance materials support good practice but do not prove this specific release satisfies the internal certification predicate.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record rather than conditionally defensible only after documentation is updated.
That the subgroup limitation has in fact been properly disclosed in the current release record.
That monitoring alone is sufficient absent approved mitigation or actual disclosure evidence.
That public governance guidance materially closes the gap in release-specific policy compliance.
